texts.preamble: Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Scch-13 1 Mvc.4138/2023 Kabc020184312023 In The Court Of Ii Addl. Small Causes Judge, Acjm And Member-Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru . (Scch-13) Dated The 28th Day Of August 2025. Present: Smt.Shyla S.M., B.B.M. Ll.B., Ii Addl.Judge & Acjm, Court of Small Causes Bengaluru M.V.C.No.4138/2023
texts.facts: This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that, on 10-03-2023 at about 4.30 p.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-JK-6756 on the left side of Jadugatte Road, proceeding from Mysuru towards Turuvekere, opposite to the Petrol Bunk at Jadugatte Gate, Mayasandra, Hobli, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkuru District. At that time, the driver of a lorry bearing Registration No. MH-38-X-5590 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle. 3. As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. His motorcycle was also extensively damaged. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G. Nagara, where he was given initial treatment. Subsequently, he was referred to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery. 4. It is further submitted that the petitioner incurred an expenditure of 23,75,000/- towards medical treatment and other incidental charges. At the time of the accident, the petitioner was aged about 20 years and was pursuing 3rd year B.E. in Computer Science at A.T.M.E. Engineering College, Mysuru. Apart from his studies, he was also assisting his father in his business and agricultural activities, thereby earning about 30,000/- per month. Due to the accident, the petitioner was unable to attend classes and work, resulting in loss of education, loss of income, and adverse impact on his future prospects. The accident occurred solely on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle. Hence, the petitioner has prayed for award of compensation of 1,00,00,000/- from the respondents 5. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. The respondent No.1 remained absent and accordingly was placed exparte. 6. Respondent No. 2, the Insurer, has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of the accident. However, it has contended that its liability, if any, is always subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy. 7. It is further contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police authorities have failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and Section 159 of the Motor Vehicles Act. The respondent has also asserted that the driver of the offending vehicle was Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/ 2 not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident, and that the vehicle did not possess a valid permit. 8. The respondent has specifically denied the allegation of rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle. On the contrary, it is contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself, as he was riding an uninsured motorcycle, without a valid driving licence, and without necessary safety measures such as a head guard. The respondent has further denied the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident, the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the avocation and income of the petitioner, the future medical expenses claimed, the medical expenditure allegedly incurred, and the disability said to have been suffered. On these grounds, Respondent No. 2 has prayed for dismissal of the petition. 10. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, 3 witnesses were examined as PW-2 to 4 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.29.
texts.arguments: It has also contended that the claim for compensation is highly exaggerated and exorbitant. 35 . Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability. Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .30,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life. 37. Future medical expenses: PW-2 has deposed that petitioner required one more surgery for removal of implant, which would cost around Rs.40,000/-. Considering the petitioner's ongoing medical needs, permanent condition, and potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards under head of future medical expenses.
